govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LevisonStanley_: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Chauncey Eskridge on Stanley Levison — May 19 — is a researcher’s note. Levison was King’s close adviser. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-McGuireMickey_M: Marsha Vande Berg’s ‘Hinted Break Interest to Interviewer’ — interview of James — is a press piece. Interviews capture the subject’s voice. The piece is a time capsule. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
a-fool-and-his-money: George Barr McCutcheon, the bestselling author of Graustark romances, spins a lighthearted tale of sudden wealth and the trouble it brings. His hero must navigate schemers, flatterers, and romantic misunderstandings as money upends his ordinary life. Written in McCutcheon's breezy, good-natured style, the novel is pure early-twentieth-century escapism — funny, romantic, and quickly paced.
locusts-and-wild-honey: John Burroughs, America's best-loved nature writer of the 1800s, gathers essays on bees, birds, and country life in this warm collection. He writes about tracking wild honeybees through the woods and watching spring return to the Catskills with the eye of a born observer. The book helped create American nature writing, teaching readers to pay close attention to the wild near home.
the-story-of-the-odyssey: Scholar Alfred Church retells Homer's great epic in clear prose for young readers. Follow Odysseus through ten years of wandering after the fall of Troy — the Cyclops, the Sirens, the long voyage home to faithful Penelope. Church keeps the wonder of the original while making the ancient tale easy to follow, a perfect first meeting with one of literature's greatest heroes.
uneasy-money: Wodehouse spins comic gold from a will with impossible conditions: Bill Dawlish inherits a fortune only if he gives up his beloved football. Meanwhile a chorus of schemers circles the money. Mistaken identities and romantic tangles pile up in this breezy tale of wealth that brings nothing but trouble.
mrs-shelley: Lucy Madox Brown Rossetti — daughter of Ford Madox Brown — writes the life of Mary Shelley for the Eminent Women series. The author of Frankenstein appears as daughter, wife, widow, and working writer, navigating scandal and sorrow with courage. A sympathetic Victorian biography of a remarkable woman.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-corv: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Corvey — the imperial abbey of Saxony, famed for its library — recounts its princely history. George Cyprian Alston details its Carolingian glory. A strong reference on German monasticism. Saxon emperors prized its scriptorium above all others.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey: This 1913 reference piece treats the abbey itself — what a monastery is, how abbots rule, and how houses grew. Henry Birt covers the whole subject with learned care. Monks, nuns, and canons all find their place here. The best one-stop guide to the monastic world.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achor-valley: A 1913 entry on the Valley of Achor — the vale of trouble, where Achan was stoned. Wendell Reilly maps its somber site. Hosea promised it as a door of hope. Judgment turned to promise. Joshua's lot fell there by the Jordan. Its stones still mark the solemn place.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anne-hanson-d: This 1913 reference piece on Anna Hanson Dorsey — the American Catholic novelist — praises her tales. Mary Waggaman wrote it up. Her pen served faith and home. Her forty books filled the parlors. Baltimore read her with love. The first lady of Catholic fiction. Her home was the town's literary salon.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anthony-champ: A 1913 entry on Anthony Champney — the English priest and controversialist. Edwin Burton notes his learned pen. His disputes defended the old faith. Douai's college formed his mind. A scholar of the mission times. His history told the mission's tale. His pen served the English mission.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anthony-rey: A 1913 entry on Anthony Rey — a Jesuit educator of note. Nicholas Weber records his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. The Society honors its teachers. A priest of the order's schools. His college trained the young clerics. His pupils filled the American colleges.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aubrey-beards: A 1913 entry on Aubrey Beardsley — the artist of the black line. George Williamson notes his brief bright career. His illustrations shocked the nineties. He died a Catholic at twenty-five. The meteor of the Yellow Book. His Salomé illustrations are famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aulne-abbey: This 1913 reference article on Aulne Abbey — the Cistercian house of Belgium. Michael Ott notes its medieval glory. Its ruins crown the Sambre's bank. The Revolution scattered its monks. A jewel of the white monks. Its brewery was the monks' delight.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bangor-abbey: This 1913 reference article on Bangor Abbey — the great Irish monastery. Edward D'Alton honors its golden age. Its monks sailed to Europe's shores. Columbanus carried its fire abroad. The light of the northern monks. Its psalter is Ireland's treasure. Its Rule shaped the Irish monks.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-barent-van-or: A 1913 entry on Barent van Orley — the Flemish master of tapestry design. George Williamson praises his Brussels works. His cartoons clothed the Vatican walls. The court painter of Margaret's Brussels. The Raphael of the Netherlands. His Job tapestries hang in the Louvre.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bath-abbey: This 1913 reference piece on Bath Abbey — the Somerset church of the healing springs. Oswald Hunter-Blair honors its fan-vaulted nave. The angels climb its western front. The monks prayed by the hot wells. England's most graceful parish church. Its west front tells in stone.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-battle-abbey: This 1913 reference piece on Battle Abbey — the Conqueror's thank-offering. Edwin Burton tells its Norman tale. Its high altar stood where Harold fell. The monks prayed for the slain. The abbey of the Hastings field. Its gatehouse guards the Sussex field.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-beaulieu-abbe: A 1913 entry on Beaulieu Abbey — the Cistercian house of the New Forest. Oswald Hunter-Blair honors its white monks. Its refectory pulpit is famed. The Dissolution scattered its brethren. A jewel of the Hampshire woods. Its precinct is now a motor museum.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-belley: This 1913 reference piece on Belley — the French diocese of the Curé of Ars. Georges Goyau honors its saintly son. Ars keeps the holy priest's shrine. The Bugey hills guard its town. A see of the eastern hills. Its shrine draws the weary pilgrims.
